About us

Massachusetts doors, Massachusetts crew

Henesys AA Inc. is a family-owned garage door company working across the Commonwealth. We handle residential and commercial doors — the 2 a.m. broken spring and the planned Saturday install alike — with our own technicians, our own trucks, and manufacturer parts rather than whatever is cheapest that week.

What that means in practice is simple. You speak to someone who knows doors when you call. You get a written price before a wrench turns. And the person who quotes the job is the person who does it.

Working process

Three steps, start to finish

No mystery pricing and no surprise line items. Here's exactly how a Henesys AA job runs.

1

Consultation

You call or send the form. We ask what the door is doing, measure and inspect on site, and put a written price in your hand before anything is opened or unbolted.

2

Professional execution

Our own technicians do the work with manufacturer parts — springs matched to the door's weight, new hardware where it's needed, and the opener set and force-tested afterwards.

3

Customer satisfaction

We balance the door by hand, cycle it with you watching, clean up the site, and leave you the warranty on parts and labour. If something isn't right, we come back.

Door styles

Pick the door, we'll handle the rest

Four families cover almost every job we do. Measured on site, priced in writing, installed with new track, springs and hardware.

Insulated Steel

The workhorse. Steel skin over a polyurethane or polystyrene core, optional top-row windows, in every standard colour.

Best for: warm garages and lower heating bills

Carriage House

Swing-door looks on a modern sectional body. Decorative strap hinges, handles and arched glass, in wood grain or painted steel.

Best for: colonials, capes and period homes

Full-View Aluminium

Anodised aluminium frame with clear, frosted or tinted glass. Daylight in the garage and the sharpest contemporary look on the street.

Best for: modern builds, studios and showrooms

Modern & Wood-Look

Flush or cedar-clad faces with narrow window bands. Real wood or a wood-grain composite over an insulated core, with no raised panels to date the house.

Best for: contemporary builds and renovations

Before you call

What the door is telling you

You can usually name the problem from the sound it made. Here's what we hear most, what it normally is, and whether it can wait until morning.

What you noticedUsually meansTypical fixUrgency
A bang like a gunshot from the garageTorsion spring snapped — the door is now its full dead weightSpring replacement, both sides, matched to door weightCall now
Door opens crooked or hangs at an angleA lift cable has slipped a drum or frayed throughCable and drum reset, re-tension both sidesCall now
Door jumped out of the trackBent track, broken roller, or a bump from a vehicleRe-seat door, straighten or replace track sectionCall now
Opener runs but the door doesn't moveStripped opener gear, sheared sprocket, or a released trolleyGear kit or opener replacementSame day
Door starts to close, then reversesPhoto-eye sensors knocked out of alignment or obstructedSensor realignment, wiring check, limit resetSame day
Loud grinding or rattling on every cycleWorn steel rollers, dry bearings, loose hingesNylon roller upgrade, hardware tightening, lubricationScheduled
Cold garage, high heating billUninsulated door, failed weather seal, gapped jambSeal replacement or insulated door quoteScheduled

One safety note: a torsion spring holds several hundred pounds of stored tension. If a spring, cable or drum is involved, leave the door where it is, don't pull the emergency release under load, and call us.

FAQ

Straight answers

How often should I have my garage door serviced?

Once a year for a door cycled a few times a day, and twice a year for a commercial door in constant use. A tune-up is a balance check, hardware tightening, roller and hinge inspection, cable and drum check, lubrication, and an opener force and safety-reverse test. It costs a fraction of the spring failure it prevents.

What are the signs my garage door needs repair?

Grinding or rattling on every cycle, a door that opens crooked or hangs at an angle, one that starts closing and reverses, jerky movement, gaps at the bottom when it's shut, or an opener straining audibly. Any of those is the door telling you something is wearing out — see the table above for what each usually means.

How long does a typical installation take?

A standard residential door replacement is about half a day, including removing and hauling away the old one. Spring and cable repairs run one to two hours. Opener replacement is usually two to three. Commercial doors depend on size and operator, and we'll give you a time along with the price.

What should I do if my door stops working suddenly?

Stop using it. If you heard a loud bang, a spring has almost certainly gone and the door is now its full dead weight — running the opener against it turns one repair into two. Don't pull the emergency release on a door under load. Park outside, leave it where it is, and call.

Can I replace one panel instead of the whole door?

Often, yes — a single dented or cracked section can be swapped if the model is still made and the rest of the door is sound. If the door is old, discontinued, or the damage bent the track and hardware too, replacement is usually the cheaper answer. We'll tell you which it is and why.

What about emergencies outside business hours?

Call the same number. Emergency service runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week — broken springs, snapped cables, doors off track and doors that won't close all get dispatched at night and on weekends.
